clue.text: Busts sergeant major, maybe, that bribes guards

indicators.note: something that guards a thing surrounds it, so the bribes word encloses the soldier

parts.note: sops are small bribes offered to placate someone
a sergeant major is one kind of WO, warrant officer

explanation.surface: A sergeant major is caught taking backhanders, and the bribes are what brings him down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busts' looks like a verb or statues but is a noun here: police raids.
explanation.definitionFit: Swoops are sudden police raids, which is what busts are in slang.

clue.text: It could make stay with British hosts healthy one

indicators.note: hosts means the two letters hold the healthy word between them

parts.note: hale means robust and healthy

explanation.surface: A healthy guest is put up by British hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stay' is not a visit but a stiffening strip in a corset, once made of baleen.
explanation.definitionFit: Corset stiffeners, called stays, were traditionally cut from baleen.

clue.text: Not keen on what certain doctors do in delivery method

parts.note: to be off something is to have gone off it, not to like it
spin doctors spin news to their side's advantage

explanation.surface: A dislike of what some medics do in the delivery room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests childbirth with doctors; it is a cricket ball delivery. Off spin is a cricket bowling style.
explanation.definitionFit: Off spin is a style of cricket bowling, a way of bowling the ball.

clue.text: Very posh? Just a bit

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
U is the old British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is very posh and is told only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou was a small French coin; not a sou means nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou, an old low-value French coin, stands for a tiny amount.

clue.text: Indian vessel turning west of a desert island

indicators.note: in an across answer, west of means placed to the left of the following pieces
the vessel word is turned round, read from right to left

parts.note: a jug is a vessel for pouring
to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Someone from India is pictured with a pot, heading west of a lonely island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes GUJ from JUG; 'desert' is the verb, not sand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or language of the western Indian state of Gujarat is Indian.

clue.text: Tenor giving concert: not heavy metal!

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
lithium, chemical symbol Li, is the lightest metal

explanation.surface: A singer performs a show but refuses to play heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Beniamino Gigli was a famous Italian operatic tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated twentieth-century Italian opera singer of that voice type.

clue.text: Criminal to be jailed after pinching university's religious text

indicators.note: pinching means taking in, so the shuffled letters hold the university letter
criminal signals that to be jailed is rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A crook will be locked up after stealing a college's holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges TO BE JAILED, and 'pinching' puts U into it. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jubilate Deo, Latin for rejoice in God, is Psalm 100 as sung in church services.

clue.text: In place of protest men turn up frequently and work

indicators.note: in a down clue turn up means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
oft is an old word for often
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Men often show up and go to work at the site of a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' is OR (other ranks), turned up to give RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters often climb onto a rooftop to make their point, so it is a site of demonstration.

clue.text: Convenience stores one no longer put up for rent

indicators.note: the convenience no longer holds one, so the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: a public convenience is a toilet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A public toilet has closed and the building now advertises vacancies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' is a link: the convenience no longer stores the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign reading to let means a property is available to rent.

clue.text: Females taking in a run, with breather out of the way

indicators.note: the two female letters take in, that is enclose, the next pieces

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, twice for the plural
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
a lung is the organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: Some women go for a jog and get out of breath somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts A and R between the two Fs, giving FARF.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere remote, distant and hard to reach is described as far-flung.

clue.text: Port illegally distilled not good

indicators.note: not good means the letter for good is removed from the word before it

parts.note: bootleg liquor is illegally made or distilled

explanation.surface: Port made in an illicit still turns out to be poor stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink; it is BOOTLE, a port town on Merseyside near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootle is a dockland town on the Mersey, so a port.

clue.text: One worked in kitchen, perhaps, putting together ginger hairdo poorly

parts.note: ginger as in vigour or zest is pep
a perm is a hairstyle set in waves or curls
poorly in British usage means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A kitchen worker puts together a red-haired cut badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger hairdo' reads as one red hairstyle, but the two words are separate pieces of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A pepper mill is a grinder turned by hand at the stove or table, a device worked in the kitchen.

clue.text: Variety of cake with bun that group may serve up at party

definitions.text: that group may serve up at party

parts.note: a rock cake is a rough-surfaced British bun-like cake
and means with, together
a roll is a small bread bun

explanation.surface: Cakes and buns are laid out for a buffet at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve up' suggests food; a band serves up music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock and roll is dance music a band might play at a party.

clue.text: Trip to Oz oddly the making of European leader once

indicators.note: oddly signals taking the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A trip to Australia is what made a former European statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Josip Broz Tito ruled Yugoslavia, a former European state, until 1980.

clue.text: Cut complaint from the airwaves

indicators.note: something broadcast over the airwaves is heard, so a word sounding like the complaint is meant

parts.note: a moan is a grumble or complaint

explanation.surface: Someone cuts short a complaint broadcast on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that has been mown has been cut.

clue.text: Happen to take first place, then a couple of seconds

parts.note: to come top is to finish first
S is the abbreviation for second, two of them here

explanation.surface: A racer manages to win, with two others a fraction of a second behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to pass is an idiom for occur, take place.

clue.text: Denied speech mostly is about slander

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the shortened word is reversed
mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: someone dumb has been denied the power to speak

explanation.surface: Most of what is said, when someone is prevented from speaking, is about libel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DUMB to DUM, and 'is about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing mud means spreading damaging accusations, smearing someone's name.

clue.text: Police dogs quiet at home: one stops barking

indicators.note: dogs means follows, so the police word trails the other pieces

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
in means at home
to police is to guard, as a verb

explanation.surface: Police dogs are kept quiet at home, and one stops them barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is not a dog's noise but knocking the shins; 'Police dogs' is not a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A shin pad protects the front of the leg from being knocked or scraped.

clue.text: Like some compliments we've gone and given?

parts.note: if we have gone, we have left
handed means given, passed over

explanation.surface: A guest leaves after paying compliments as they depart.
explanation.walkthrough: A left-handed compliment is a backhanded one that is really an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-handed compliment is a backhanded one, praise with a sting in it.

clue.text: When buying new suit one should be bold

definitions.text: When buying new suit one should

explanation.surface: Advice when shopping for clothes: be daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers should put a suit on before buying; separately, the idiom means chance one's arm, test someone's limits.

clue.text: Catch carp, mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to carp is to complain, to gripe

explanation.surface: An angler's catch is mostly carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' looks like the fish but is the verb meaning complain.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a hold or grasp, which a catch also is.

clue.text: Characters in tragedy originally did turns

indicators.note: originally implies the letters were once arranged otherwise, so tragedy is reordered

explanation.surface: The actors in a tragedy first performed pirouettes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges the letters of TRAGEDY. 'Characters in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or rotate, so it means revolved.

clue.text: Son means to acquire influence

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: A son uses his resources to gain sway over others.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have power or control over something.

clue.text: Opposite wings and extremes abandoning Tories, to give balance

parts.note: the west and east wings of a building face each other, W and E

indicators.note: the outer letters leave, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: the right is the political wing of the Tories

explanation.surface: Both political wings shed their extremists after the Tories leave, to restore balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes abandoning' strips the first and last letters from RIGHT, giving IGH. 'to give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh up options is to balance them against each other.

clue.text: Desire to pen article after party gets put off

indicators.note: the desire piece follows the party word in the answer

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the desire word holds the article

parts.note: an urge is a strong desire
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Wanting to write something after a party leaves someone deterred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pen' means enclose, not write; 'gets' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to dissuade or deter them, just as putting them off does.

clue.text: What Sandra Foster from South Shields is up to now

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming from the south means reading upwards, backwards
the name shields, that is conceals, the letters within it

explanation.surface: A Geordie woman from South Shields describes how far she has got.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shields' hides RAFOS in SANDRA FOSTER, and 'from South' reads it upwards. South Shields is a town in north-east England; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: So far is an idiom for until the present moment.

clue.text: Life captures celebrity leaving a restaurant

indicators.note: captures means the life word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story

indicators.note: leaving a means the letter A goes out of the celebrity word

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Life magazine features a famous person walking out of an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Life reads as the magazine, but it simply means a biography here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal French-style eating place.

clue.text: Lead singer's pants torn, minutes after being grabbed by groupie

indicators.note: being grabbed by the groupie means being held inside that word

parts.note: a groupie is a devoted fan

indicators.note: the letter for minutes comes after the shuffled letters
pants as slang for rubbish signals that torn is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock singer's trousers rip when a fan grabs him moments later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, here the anagram signal; the 's stands for 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontman is the main performer who fronts a band, usually its singer.

clue.text: Hooter — it and others — loudly going off

indicators.note: going off means leaving, so the loudly letter is removed

parts.note: fowl as a collective noun means birds
F is forte, the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: A car horn and others are sounding loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn; it is an owl, a bird that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl hoots, so it is a natural crossword hooter.

clue.text: Dealer supplying shipment caught by officer with dog?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a police dog handler is an officer working with a dog

explanation.surface: A drug dealer is arrested by a police officer and his sniffer dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship's chandler sells provisions and gear for vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's chandler is a merchant who sells supplies for boats.

clue.text: Line suited those who'd be dry without becoming pretentious

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dry group surrounds the next word

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is for people trying to stay off drink
did as in that did nicely, meaning suited

explanation.surface: A line of clothing suited to teetotallers is somehow pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside; 'suited' as DID is a stretch (that did nicely). 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes affected, posh manners, a snooty pretension.
